::: {.callout-tip}
## Why This Matters
The starkest case of a US export-control action landing directly on a named facility: added to the Entity List in October 2018 amid a Micron trade-secret theft dispute involving JHICC and Taiwan's UMC, just as its DRAM line was nearing production.
:::

**Chinese name:** 晋华集成电路 (Jìnhuá Jíchéng Diànlù)

## What does this facility make?

DRAM chips on 12-inch (300mm) wafers, planned capacity of 60,000 wafers/month.

## Why does it matter?

Widely reported as crippled by the 2018 ban in the years immediately after — a criminal case against JHICC and UMC followed, later resolved without a conviction against JHICC. More recent reporting describes the fab holding roughly 40,000 wafers/month of stable capacity with plans to expand toward 60,000 by 2026, a status this tracker could not fully reconcile against the earlier 'crippled' narrative — treat the current production figure as provisional pending a dedicated follow-up source check.
